land.text: the whole country: the Democratic Republic of Afghanistan, 'Established: 30 April 1978' after the Saur Revolution of 27-28 April 1978

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Afghanistan row starts in 1979; its Republic of Afghanistan row runs to 1978. The republic-of-afghanistan dossier asks this one to begin on 30 April 1978.

capitals.name: Kabul
capitals.note: Infobox: Kabul 34°31'N 69°11'E. The Islamic State's capital was Kabul 1992-1996 (Islamic State page infobox).

capitals.name: Taloqan, capital in exile of the Islamic State and the Northern Alliance
capitals.note: Infobox 'Taloqan (1996-2000)'; coordinates from the gazetteer's Natural Earth place. The Taliban held Kabul 1996-2001 (taliban dossier).

capitals.name: Kabul
capitals.note: 'Kabul retaken: 13 November 2001'; the capital since (Afghanistan page infobox).

correction.text: the whole country, as the Democratic Republic claimed it from 30 April 1978

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Afghanistan row starts in 1979 but the Democratic Republic was established on 30 April 1978 ('Saur Revolution: 27-28 April 1978', 'Established: 30 April 1978'). The Republic of Afghanistan row's 1976 outline (the whole country) is used for 1978; that row also runs to 1978, so the year is drawn once by each dossier. Infobox area 652,864 km2 (Afghanistan and Democratic Republic pages).

correction.text: the whole country as the Democratic Republic claimed it: infobox area 652,864 km2, capital Kabul

keyframe_review.note: 537,138 km2 against the infobox 652,864 km2 (ratio 0.82, within a factor of two, but the shape is the wrong shape). A gazetteer overlay on Natural Earth provinces puts only 2 of the 16 grid cells of Kabul province, the capital named in the infobox, inside the shape, and leaves out large parts of Parwan, Laghman, Nangarhar, Kapisa, Wardak and Zabul. The page makes the state the whole country under Soviet occupation (1979-1989); the mujahideen's 'almost 80 percent' is a layer (ledger contest_start, occupation_start), not a hole in the state. Corrected to the 2006 outline (643,926 km2, ratio 0.99).

correction.text: the whole country as the Democratic Republic claimed it: infobox area 652,864 km2

keyframe_review.note: 582,468 km2 (ratio 0.89 of the infobox). Same fault as the 1979 shape: Kabul province only 7 of 16 cells inside, northern provinces (Baghlan, Kunduz, Faryab, Balkh) partly out, no page that supports a government-held outline. Corrected to the whole country; the real control is the ledger's contest with the mujahideen (1979-1992).

correction.text: the nominal territory of the Republic of Afghanistan (Najibullah), of which the government 'controlled only 10 percent' by the beginning of 1991

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1987-1991: Cliopatria has no Afghanistan shape for 1987-1995 and draws the whole country as 'Mujahideen' (587,000 km2 in 1987-89, 644,005 km2 in 1990-91, which also covers Kabul). The government still held Kabul until 28 April 1992 ('Fall of Kabul: 28 April 1992'), but no page gives its holdings as land: 'By the beginning of 1991, the government controlled only 10 percent of Afghanistan' and 'the government lost control of the countryside'. Kept as the nominal whole country, contested with the mujahideen (ledger contest 1979-1992); the mujahideen dossier carries the rebel-held outline without Kabul.

correction.text: the whole country as the Islamic State of Afghanistan, April 1992 to 1996

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1992-1995: Cliopatria draws these years as 'Mujahideen' (643,926 km2, the same outline as the 2006 Afghanistan shape) while the pages make it the Islamic State of Afghanistan ('established in April 1992 under the Peshawar Accord', 'State proclaimed: 28 April 1992', capital Kabul 1992-1996). It is the same state as this dossier, so the outline is claimed here (and marked wrong in the mujahideen dossier). Factional fighting (Hekmatyar clashing with Rabbani's troops, 'Kabul was largely destroyed') and the Taliban from late 1994 (large parts of the south) move no outline that a page can place; they are ledger contests.

correction.text: unchanged outline, valid for 1996-1997 only: the north and northeast left to the Islamic State and the United Front after the Taliban took Kabul in September 1996

keyframe_review.note: 192,790 km2 (29.5% of the infobox area): the north and northeast, which matches the Taliban at Kabul in September 1996 ('by the end of the year occupying two-thirds of Afghanistan') and the Northern Alliance page's 'roughly 30% of Afghanistan's population'. Outline unchanged; the years change: it is right from the autumn of 1996 to the fall of Mazar-i-Sharif (8 August 1998); before 27 September 1996 the Islamic State still held Kabul (see afghanistan_1992), and from August 1998 the Balkh plain is gone (afghanistan_1998). Cliopatria's Taliban row (450,887 km2 in 1996-99) is the complement. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1996..1997 from this entry's own 'valid for 1996-1997 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: the 1996 outline without the Balkh plain around Mazar-i-Sharif, taken by the Taliban on 8 August 1998

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1998-1999: '...finally Mazar-i-Sharif (8 August 1998)' fell to the Taliban (the Northern Alliance page says 'overrun in 1997' and 'defeated by the Taliban and their allies in 1998'). Cliopatria keeps the 192,790 km2 shape to 1999 and drops the north only in 2000. Balkh is removed from the 1996 outline; the pages do not give the rest of the 1998-1999 front, so the other provinces stay (a gap-filler should open the Battle of Mazar-i-Sharif pages).

correction.text: the northeast, without Taloqan (taken by the Taliban on 5 September 2000), valid for 2000-2001

keyframe_review.note: 83,240 km2 (12.7% of the infobox area): the northeast, in line with 'By 2000, the Northern Alliance only controlled 10% of the territory, cornered in the northeast' (Afghanistan page) and 'by 2001, controlled only about 5% of the country' (Northern Alliance page). Valid for 2000-2001 only; Taloqan, in the Takhar part of the outline, fell on 5 September 2000 and the headquarters moved to Badakhshan, so it is cut out. From December 2001 the shape is wrong: see afghanistan_2002. Cliopatria carries it to 2005. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 2000..2001 from this entry's own 'Valid for 2000-2001 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: the whole country under the Interim Administration (22 December 2001), the Transitional Islamic State (June 2002) and the Islamic Republic (January 2004)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 2002-2005: after 'The Northern Alliance drove the Taliban away in December 2001' (Kabul retaken 13 November 2001) the Afghan Interim Administration took office on 22 December 2001 (Afghan Interim Government URL), the Transitional Islamic State followed on 19 June 2002 and the Islamic Republic on 26 January 2004. The state is the whole country; Cliopatria's 83,240 km2 Northern Alliance shape to 2005 and its Taliban row to 2005 (560,314 km2) are both too long. The Taliban insurgency's lands for 2002-2005 are on none of the pages.

643,926 km2 against the infobox 652,864 km2 (ratio 0.99). Whole country under the Islamic Republic (constitution of 2004); on 15 August 2021 'The Taliban captured the capital city of Kabul', a change of regime that leaves the outline as it is (ledger rename).
Same outline as 2006-2023; the Islamic Emirate 'Restoration of Islamic Emirate: 15 August 2021' governs the whole country.

region.text: the whole country, from the Republic of Afghanistan of Daoud (1973-1978)

ledger.note: 1978: the PDPA proclaims the Democratic Republic of Afghanistan at Kabul. 'Saur Revolution: 27–28 April 1978' and 'Established: 30 April 1978'; Nur Muhammad Taraki 'succeeded' Daoud 'as the head of state and government on 30 April 1978'.

region.text: 'Afghanistan's major cities and all main arteries of communication'; extent is the researcher's reading as the page names no city

ledger.note: 1979: the Soviet 40th Army enters Afghanistan. 'The Soviet 40th Army launched its initial incursion into Afghanistan on 25 December' and 'On 27 December 1979, 700 Soviet troops dressed in Afghan uniforms' took key sites in Kabul; 'Soviet troops occupied Afghanistan's major cities and all main arteries of communication'. Over 100,000 men, about 115,000 by the mid-1980s. The Democratic Republic page gives 25 December in its infobox and 27 December in its text. Hatched, not a change of owner.

region.text: the countryside: 'Almost 80 percent of the country was outside government control'

ledger.note: 1979: the mujahideen war against the government and the Soviets begins. 'Almost 80 percent of the country was outside government control'; the war runs 25 December 1979 to 15 February 1989 (infobox). The page does not date the first uprisings, so the year is the war's. The mujahideen dossier's Cliopatria shapes start in 1987.

1987: the Democratic Republic becomes the Republic of Afghanistan. The page says the state was 'later known as the Republic of Afghanistan' and dates the loya jirga of the 1987 constitution to 29/30 November 1987, but does not say the name changed then; the Afghanistan page lists no 1987 entry. Same state, same colour (rule 2).
15 February 1989: the last Soviet troops leave. 'On 15 February 1989, the last Soviet military column occupying Afghanistan crossed into the Uzbek SSR.'

region.text: the countryside held by the mujahideen

ledger.note: 28 April 1992: Kabul falls to the mujahideen. Najibullah 'was forced to resign by 4 of his generals' on 14 April; infobox 'Fall of Kabul: 28 April 1992'. 'By the beginning of 1991, the government controlled only 10 percent of Afghanistan'. The page lists the Islamic State of Afghanistan as successor.

region.text: the whole country as the Islamic State of Afghanistan

ledger.note: 1992: the mujahideen coalition takes the state. The Islamic State of Afghanistan 'was established in April 1992 under the Peshawar Accord' (infobox 'State proclaimed: 28 April 1992'); the Accord is dated 25 April in the text and 24 April in the infobox. The land is the whole country (Cliopatria's 'Mujahideen' 1992 shape, 643,926 km2), which the page does not outline.
28 April 1992: the Republic of Afghanistan becomes the Islamic State of Afghanistan, with Kabul as capital until 1996. Same state, same colour; an era caption (rule 2).

region.text: 'large parts of southern Afghanistan' (the page names no province)

ledger.note: Late 1994: the Taliban take the south. In 'late 1994' they 'managed to conquer large parts of southern Afghanistan' and made 'steady gains throughout 1995 and 1996'. The page names no province (Kandahar and Herat are not on it); the four southern provinces are the researcher's reading.

region.text: 'large parts of southern Afghanistan' (the page names no province)

ledger.note: September 1996: the southern contest ends in the Taliban capture of Kabul; the front moves north (next event).

region.text: Kabul and 'two-thirds of Afghanistan' by the end of 1996

ledger.note: 27 September 1996: the Taliban take Kabul. 'the Taliban were able to seize control of the capital city of Kabul in September 1996' (infobox 'Taliban capture Kabul: 27 September 1996') and by the end of the year occupied 'two-thirds of Afghanistan'. Land = Cliopatria's Taliban shape of 1996 (450,887 km2), the complement of this state's 192,790 km2.
1996: the Islamic State's government withdraws to Taloqan (capital in exile 1996-2000; infobox).

region.text: the front line between the Taliban and the United Front (Northern Alliance), 1996-2001

ledger.note: September 1996: the Northern Alliance forms against the Taliban. 'The group was founded in September 1996, following the Taliban's takeover of Kabul'; 'From the Taliban conquest of Kabul in September 1996 until November 2001 the United Front controlled roughly 30% of Afghanistan's population', provinces Badakhshan, Kapisa, Takhar. The page gives no front line; the band between the two Cliopatria shapes is the researcher's reading.

8 August 1998: the Taliban take Mazar-i-Sharif. '...finally Mazar-i-Sharif (8 August 1998)'; the Northern Alliance page says the city 'was overrun in 1997' and its forces 'were defeated by the Taliban and their allies in 1998'. Balkh is the researcher's reading of the city's land; Cliopatria drops the north from its shape only in 2000.

region.text: the city of Taloqan and its district

ledger.note: 5 September 2000: the Taliban take Taloqan. '...until September 5, 2000, when the city was taken by the Taliban'; the headquarters moved to Badakhshan (Fayzabad, capital in exile 2000-2001). 'By 2000, the Northern Alliance only controlled 10% of the territory, cornered in the northeast' (Afghanistan page).
2000: the capital in exile moves from Taloqan to Fayzabad (infobox 'Fayzabad (2000-2001)').

13 November 2001: Kabul is retaken. Infobox 'Kabul retaken: 13 November 2001'; the Northern Alliance page: 'With the fall of Kabul to anti-Taliban forces in November 2001'. Kabul is again the capital (infobox 'Kabul (1992-1996, 2001-2002)').
November 2001: the government returns to Kabul.

region.text: the Taliban's territory, taken over by the Northern Alliance and the new administration

ledger.note: December 2001: the Taliban are driven from power. 'The Northern Alliance drove the Taliban away in December 2001' (Afghanistan page: US invasion in October 2001, 'the Taliban regime came to an end'). Land = Cliopatria's Taliban shape of 2000 (560,314 km2).

region.text: the front line between the Taliban and the United Front (Northern Alliance), 1996-2001

ledger.note: December 2001: the Taliban-Alliance front ends with the fall of the Taliban regime.

22 December 2001: the Afghan Interim Administration under Hamid Karzai takes office. It 'was the highest authority of the country from 22 December 2001 until 13 June 2002'; established by the Bonn Agreement. Same state, same colour.

19 June 2002: the Transitional Islamic State of Afghanistan. Infobox 'Transitional Islamic State of Afghanistan established: 19 June 2002' (the Interim Administration page ends its term on 13 June 2002).
26 January 2004: the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan. Infobox 'Islamic Republic: 26 January 2004'; 'adopting a constitution in 2004 with the name Islamic Republic of Afghanistan'.

15 August 2021: the Taliban return to power at Kabul. 'The Taliban captured the capital city of Kabul on 15 August 2021'; infobox 'Restoration of Islamic Emirate: 15 August 2021'. The whole country, one outline; the taliban dossier covers only the Cliopatria row of 1996-2005.

wars.name: Soviet–Afghan War

zones.text: the whole country: 'Almost 80 percent of the country was outside government control'

wars.outcome: Infobox result 'Afghan mujahideen victory', 25 December 1979 to 15 February 1989. The Soviets withdrew; the government fell in 1992.
wars.note: A 1989 mujahideen siege of Jalalabad was broken by the government (see the mujahideen dossier).

wars.name: Afghan civil war, 1992-1996 (as told on the Islamic State of Afghanistan page)

zones.text: 'large parts of southern Afghanistan' (the page names no province)

wars.outcome: Rabbani's government lost Kabul to the Taliban in September 1996 and withdrew to the north; the Taliban held 'two-thirds of Afghanistan' by the end of 1996.
wars.note: The page gives no fief lines for the factions.

wars.name: Taliban–Northern Alliance war, 1996-2001

zones.text: the front line between the Taliban and the United Front (Northern Alliance), 1996-2001

wars.outcome: The Alliance shrank from about 30% of the population (1996) to 'only about 5% of the country' (2001) and returned with Kabul in November 2001.

wars.name: War in Afghanistan (2001-2021)

zones.text: 'The Taliban captured the capital city of Kabul on 15 August 2021, after regaining control over a vast majority of Afghanistan'

wars.outcome: In October 2001 'the United States invaded Afghanistan to remove the Taliban from power'; the Taliban regime ended in December 2001; the Islamic Republic fell when 'The Taliban captured the capital city of Kabul on 15 August 2021'. No outline change that the pages date for 2002-2020.
wars.note: Zone added by the reviewer: ground changed hands in 2021, when the Taliban regained 'a vast majority of Afghanistan' before taking Kabul on 15 August 2021 (Afghanistan page). The page gives no controlled-land figures for 2002-2020 and no start month for the 2021 offensive, so the ledger has no contest pair for it.

certainty.note: Judgement: the outer frontier is the modern international boundary and the pages opened discuss no survey or treaty line (the Durand Line is not on them). The war's fronts are ledger contests, not borders.
The Taliban-Alliance front moved with each offensive (Mazar-i-Sharif 1998, Taloqan 2000) and the pages give only percentages, so the Alliance's edge is soft.
Whole-country outline; the same judgement as for 1978-1995.

notes: Six pages were opened against a budget of up to 5 (the sixth, the Afghan Interim Government URL, served the 2001 Interim Administration and gave one date). Cliopatria quirks: (1) the Afghanistan row has no shape for 1987-1995 and the 'Mujahideen' row fills those years with the whole country (587k, 644k and 644k km2); this dossier takes the government's side as new keyframes afghanistan_1987 (nominal whole country, contested) and afghanistan_1992 (the Islamic State, the same outline as 'Mujahideen' 1992), and marks mujahideen_1992 wrong in the mujahideen dossier. (2) The 1979 and 1983 shapes (537k, 582k) have holes at Kabul and the east; corrected to the whole country. (3) The 1996-1999 and 2000-2005 shapes are the Northern Alliance rump (Islamic State of Afghanistan in exile) and the Taliban row 'Taliban' 1996-2005 is its complement; both run four years past the Taliban's fall in December 2001, so afghanistan_2002 puts the whole country back from 2002. (4) The Wikidata id Q889 is shared by emirate-of-afghanistan, kingdom-of-afghanistan, republic-of-afghanistan and this row. The state is one in Wikipedia's reckoning; the other ia-03 parts wrote the earlier regimes as separate dossiers and republic-of-afghanistan names this one as its successor, so this dossier covers 30 April 1978 onward and does not merge them. Not settled within the budget: the extents of the 1998-1999 front (only Balkh is cut), the Jan-Sep 1996 Islamic State territory, Taliban lands 2002-2005, the Durand Line, Wakhan, and the factional fiefs of 1992-1996 (the Islamic State page names no province). The mujahideen are written as a rebel dossier (type rebel) with counterpart 'mujahideen'; the Taliban counterpart string is 'taliban', a row another ia-03 part writes. Hezb-e Islami and Hizb-i-Wahdat appear only as names in the civil-war entry. Region names the gazetteer resolves: all (Balkh, Kabul, Taloqan, Kandahar, Hilmand, Zabul, Uruzgan, border_band afghanistan|taliban 1996 resolves with 389 cells).
